1.text_clean:
1. A student measures the length $l$ and width $w$ of a rectangular table top.
What is the absolute uncertainty of the perimeter of the table top?
[Diagram: rectangle with $l = (10.0 \pm 0.1)$ cm along one side and $w = (20.0 \pm 0.2)$ cm along the other]
A. 0.3 cm
B. 0.6 cm
C. 1.2 cm
D. 2.4 cm

2.text_clean:
2. The minute hand of a clock hanging on a vertical wall has length $L = 30$ cm.
[Diagram: clock face with the minute hand pointing at 12; P is the tip of the hand, length L]
The minute hand is observed pointing at 12 and then again 30 minutes later when the minute hand is pointing at 6.
What is the average velocity and average speed of point P on the minute hand during this time interval?
Average velocity | Average speed
A. 2 cm min$^{-1}$ vertically downwards | $\pi$ cm min$^{-1}$
B. 2 cm min$^{-1}$ vertically upwards | $\pi$ cm min$^{-1}$
C. $2\pi$ cm min$^{-1}$ vertically downwards | $2\pi$ cm min$^{-1}$
D. $2\pi$ cm min$^{-1}$ vertically upwards | $2\pi$ cm min$^{-1}$

3.text_clean:
3. A block rests on a rough horizontal plane. A force P is applied to the block and the block moves to the right.
[Diagram: block on a horizontal surface, force P to the right, frictional force F to the left]
There is a coefficient of friction $\mu_d$ giving rise to a frictional force F between the block and the plane. The force P is doubled. Will $\mu_d$ and F be unchanged or greater?
$\mu_d$ | F
A. unchanged | unchanged
B. unchanged | greater
C. greater | greater
D. greater | unchanged

4.text_clean:
4. A projectile is launched at an angle above the horizontal with a horizontal component of velocity $V_h$ and a vertical component of velocity $V_v$. Air resistance is negligible. Which graphs show the variation with time of $V_h$ and of $V_v$?
[Graphs: four pairs of $V_h$–t and $V_v$–t graphs.
A. $V_h$ decreasing linearly from positive to negative; $V_v$ constant positive.
B. $V_h$ decreasing linearly from zero to negative; $V_v$ concave-down curve starting positive and crossing zero.
C. $V_h$ concave-down curve starting positive; $V_v$ decreasing linearly from positive to negative.
D. $V_h$ constant positive; $V_v$ decreasing linearly from positive to negative.]

5.text_clean:
5. A person with a weight of 600 N stands on a scale in an elevator.
[Diagram: person standing on a scale inside an elevator]
What is the acceleration of the elevator when the scale reads 900 N?
A. 5.0 m s$^{-2}$ downwards
B. 1.5 m s$^{-2}$ downwards
C. 1.5 m s$^{-2}$ upwards
D. 5.0 m s$^{-2}$ upwards

6.text_clean:
6. Two identical blocks, each of mass $m$ and speed $v$, travel towards each other on a frictionless surface.
[Diagram: two blocks of mass m moving towards each other, each with speed v]
The blocks undergo a head-on collision. What is definitely true immediately after the collision?
A. The momentum of each block is zero.
B. The total momentum is zero.
C. The momentum of each block is $2mv$.
D. The total momentum is $2mv$.

7.text_clean:
7. The graph shows the variation with distance of a horizontal force acting on an object. The object, initially at rest, moves horizontally through a distance of 50 m.
[Graph: horizontal force / N (0–90) against distance / m (0–50); three triangular pulses each of height 80 N and base 5 m, at 0–5 m, 20–25 m and 35–40 m; force zero elsewhere]
A constant frictional force of 2.0 N opposes the motion. What is the final kinetic energy of the object after it has moved 50 m?
A. 100 J
B. 500 J
C. 600 J
D. 1100 J

8.text_clean:
8. A sample of oxygen gas with a volume of 3.0 m$^3$ is at 100 °C. The gas is heated so that it expands at a constant pressure to a final volume of 6.0 m$^3$. What is the final temperature of the gas?
A. 750 °C
B. 470 °C
C. 370 °C
D. 200 °C

9.text_clean:
9. Two identical containers X and Y each contain an ideal gas. X has $N$ molecules of gas at an absolute temperature of $T$ and Y has $3N$ molecules of gas at an absolute temperature of $\frac{T}{2}$. What is the ratio of the pressures $\frac{P_Y}{P_X}$?
[Diagram: two identical containers labelled X and Y]
A. $\frac{1}{6}$
B. $\frac{2}{3}$
C. $\frac{3}{2}$
D. 6

10.text_clean:
10. A piece of metal at a temperature of 100 °C is dropped into an equal mass of water at a temperature of 15 °C in a container of negligible mass. The specific heat capacity of water is four times that of the metal. What is the final temperature of the mixture?
A. 83 °C
B. 57 °C
C. 45 °C
D. 32 °C

11.text_clean:
11. The bob of a pendulum has an initial displacement $x_0$ to the right. The bob is released and allowed to oscillate. The graph shows how the displacement varies with time. At which point is the velocity of the bob at its maximum magnitude directed towards the left?
[Graph: displacement against time, cosine curve starting at $x_0$; A on the axis where displacement crosses zero going upwards, B at a positive maximum, C on the axis where displacement crosses zero going downwards, D at a negative minimum]

12.text_clean:
12. Which graph shows the variation of amplitude with intensity for a wave?
[Graphs: amplitude against intensity, all from the origin. A: increasing curve with decreasing gradient (concave down). B: increasing curve with increasing gradient (concave up). C: straight line through the origin. D: decreasing curve approaching zero (inverse-type)]
12.note: Official key B, but intensity is proportional to amplitude squared, so amplitude is proportional to sqrt(intensity): an increasing concave-down curve from the origin, i.e. graph A. Graph B shows amplitude proportional to intensity squared.

13.text_clean:
13. Unpolarized light of intensity $I_1$ is incident on a polarizer. The light that passes through this polarizer then passes through a second polarizer.
[Diagram: unpolarized incident light $I_1$ passes through a first polarizer, then a rotatable second polarizer, giving emergent light]
The second polarizer can be rotated to vary the intensity of the emergent light. What is the maximum value of the intensity emerging from the second polarizer?
A. $\frac{I_1}{4}$
B. $\frac{I_1}{2}$
C. $\frac{2I_1}{3}$
D. $I_1$

14.text_clean:
14. The frequency of the first harmonic in a pipe is measured. An adjustment is then made which causes the speed of sound in the pipe to increase. What is true for the frequency and the wavelength of the first harmonic when the speed of sound has increased?
Frequency | Wavelength
A. increase | unchanged
B. unchanged | increase
C. increase | increase
D. unchanged | unchanged

15.text_clean:
15. The diagram shows two cylindrical wires, X and Y. Wire X has a length $l$, a diameter $d$, and a resistivity $\rho$. Wire Y has a length $2l$, a diameter of $\frac{d}{2}$ and a resistivity of $\frac{\rho}{2}$.
[Diagram: wire X of length l and diameter d; wire Y of length 2l and diameter d/2]
What is $\frac{\text{resistance of X}}{\text{resistance of Y}}$?
A. 4
B. 2
C. 0.5
D. 0.25

16.text_clean:
16. An ion moves in a circle in a uniform magnetic field. Which single change would increase the radius of the circular path?
A. Decreasing the speed of the ion
B. Increasing the charge of the ion
C. Increasing the mass of the ion
D. Increasing the strength of the magnetic field

17.text_clean:
17. A circuit contains a variable resistor of maximum resistance R and a fixed resistor, also of resistance R, connected in series. The emf of the battery is 6.0 V and its internal resistance is negligible.
[Circuit: 6.0 V battery in series with fixed resistor R and variable resistor (0–R); voltmeter V connected across the fixed resistor R]
What are the initial and final voltmeter readings when the variable resistor is increased from an initial resistance of zero to a final resistance of R?
Initial voltmeter reading / V | Final voltmeter reading / V
A. 0 | 6.0
B. 6.0 | 0
C. 6.0 | 3.0
D. 3.0 | 6.0

18.text_clean:
18. Magnetic field lines are an example of
A. a discovery that helps us understand magnetism.
B. a model to aid in visualization.
C. a pattern in data from experiments.
D. a theory to explain concepts in magnetism.
18.note: Nature-of-science item about field lines as a model; tagged D.2.

19.text_clean:
19. An object moves in a circle of constant radius. Values of the centripetal force $F$ are measured for different values of angular velocity $\omega$. A graph is plotted with $\omega$ on the $x$-axis. Which quantity plotted on the $y$-axis will produce a straight-line graph?
A. $\sqrt{F}$
B. $F$
C. $F^2$
D. $\frac{1}{F}$

20.text_clean:
20. A sample of a pure radioactive nuclide initially contains $N_0$ atoms. The initial activity of the sample is $A_0$.
A second sample of the same nuclide initially contains $2N_0$ atoms.
What is the activity of the second sample after three half lives?
A. $\frac{A_0}{2}$
B. $\frac{A_0}{4}$
C. $\frac{A_0}{6}$
D. $\frac{A_0}{8}$

21.text_clean:
21. The diagram below shows four energy levels for the atoms of a gas. The diagram is drawn to scale. The wavelengths of the photons emitted by the energy transitions between levels are shown.
[Diagram: four energy levels; $\lambda_3$ small transition from top level to second level; $\lambda_2$ from second to third level; $\lambda_1$ from third level to lowest level; $\lambda_4$ from second level to lowest level]
What are the wavelengths of spectral lines, emitted by the gas, in order of decreasing frequency?
A. $\lambda_3, \lambda_2, \lambda_1, \lambda_4$
B. $\lambda_4, \lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3$
C. $\lambda_4, \lambda_3, \lambda_2, \lambda_1$
D. $\lambda_4, \lambda_2, \lambda_1, \lambda_3$

22.text_clean:
22. During the nuclear fission of nucleus X into nucleus Y and nucleus Z, energy is released. The binding energies per nucleon of X, Y and Z are $B_X$, $B_Y$ and $B_Z$ respectively. What is true about the binding energy per nucleon of X, Y and Z?
A. $B_Y > B_X$ and $B_Z > B_X$
B. $B_X = B_Y$ and $B_X = B_Z$
C. $B_X > B_Y$ and $B_X > B_Z$
D. $B_X = B_Y + B_Z$

23.text_clean:
23. Consider the Feynman diagram below.
[Feynman diagram: $e^-$ and $e^+$ meet at a vertex, exchange particle X (wavy line) travels to a second vertex producing $\mu^-$ and $\mu^+$; time arrow to the right]
What is the exchange particle X?
A. Lepton
B. Gluon
C. Meson
D. Photon

24.text_clean:
24. What is the main role of carbon dioxide in the greenhouse effect?
A. It absorbs incoming radiation from the Sun.
B. It absorbs outgoing radiation from the Earth.
C. It reflects incoming radiation from the Sun.
D. It reflects outgoing radiation from the Earth.

25.text_clean:
25. A model of an ideal wind turbine with blade length $l_0$ is designed to produce a power $P$ when the average wind speed is $v$. A second ideal wind turbine is designed to produce a power $\frac{P}{2}$ when the average wind speed is $\frac{v}{2}$. What is the blade length for the second wind turbine?
A. $\frac{l_0}{2}$
B. $l_0$
C. $2l_0$
D. $4l_0$

26.text_clean:
26. A mass–spring system oscillates vertically with a period of $T$ at the surface of the Earth. The gravitational field strength at the surface of Mars is $0.3g$. What is the period of the same mass–spring system on the surface of Mars?
A. $0.09T$
B. $0.3T$
C. $T$
D. $3T$

27.text_clean:
27. Light passes through a diffraction grating. Which quantity must be decreased to improve the resolution of the diffraction grating?
A. The grating spacing
B. The number of grating lines illuminated by the light source
C. The number of grating lines per millimetre
D. The spectral order being observed

28.text_clean:
28. A train is moving in a straight line away from a stationary observer when the train horn emits a sound of frequency $f_0$. The speed of the train is $0.10v$ where $v$ is the speed of sound. What is the frequency of the horn as heard by the observer?
A. $\frac{0.9}{1} f_0$
B. $\frac{1}{1.1} f_0$
C. $\frac{1.1}{1} f_0$
D. $\frac{1}{0.9} f_0$

29.text_clean:
29. Monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$ passes through a single-slit of width $b$ and produces a diffraction pattern on a screen. Which combination of changes to $b$ and $\lambda$ will cause the greatest decrease in the width of the central maximum?
Slit width | Wavelength of light
A. $\frac{1}{2}b$ | $\frac{1}{2}\lambda$
B. $\frac{1}{2}b$ | $2\lambda$
C. $2b$ | $\frac{1}{2}\lambda$
D. $2b$ | $2\lambda$

30.text_clean:
30. An object of mass $m$ released from rest near the surface of a planet has an initial acceleration $z$. What is the gravitational field strength near the surface of the planet?
A. $z$
B. $\frac{z}{m}$
C. $mz$
D. $\frac{m}{z}$

31.text_clean:
31. The points X and Y are in a uniform electric field of strength $E$. The distance OX is $x$ and the distance OY is $y$.
[Diagram: horizontal uniform field lines E pointing right; X is a distance x to the left of O along a field line; Y is a distance y vertically above O, perpendicular to the field]
What is the magnitude of the change in electric potential between X and Y?
A. $Ex$
B. $Ey$
C. $E(x + y)$
D. $E\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}$

32.text_clean:
32. A satellite orbits planet X with a speed $v_x$ at a distance r from the centre of planet X. Another satellite orbits planet Y at a speed of $v_y$ at a distance r from the centre of planet Y. The mass of planet X is $M$ and the mass of planet Y is $4M$. What is the ratio of $\frac{v_x}{v_y}$?
A. 0.25
B. 0.5
C. 2.0
D. 4.0

33.text_clean:
33. A parallel-plate capacitor is connected to a cell of constant emf. The capacitor plates are then moved closer together without disconnecting the cell. What are the changes in the capacitance of the capacitor and the energy stored in the capacitor?
Capacitance | Energy
A. increases | increases
B. increases | decreases
C. decreases | decreases
D. decreases | increases

34.text_clean:
34. The graph shows the variation of an alternating current with time in a 4.0 Ω resistor.
[Graph: sinusoidal alternating current / A against time, peak values +2.0 and −2.0, one full cycle]
What is the average power dissipated in the resistor?
A. 4 W
B. 8 W
C. 16 W
D. 32 W

35.text_clean:
35. A magnet connected to a spring oscillates above a solenoid with a 240 turn coil as shown.
[Diagram: bar magnet (N up, S down) hanging from a spring, oscillating vertically above a solenoid with 240 turn coil; solenoid connected in series with an ammeter A and a resistor]
The graph below shows the variation with time $t$ of the emf across the solenoid with the period, $T$, of the system shown.
[Graph: emf V against t, sinusoid with amplitude $V_0$, period T]
The spring is replaced with one that allows the magnet to oscillate with a higher frequency. Which graph shows the new variation with time $t$ of the current $I$ in the resistor for this new set-up?
[Graphs: I against t with reference levels $\pm I_0$ and time T marked.
A. shorter period than T, peak greater than $I_0$.
B. period T, peak $I_0$.
C. longer period, peak greater than $I_0$.
D. shorter period than T, peak $I_0$.]

36.text_clean:
36. A capacitor is charged with a constant current $I$. The graph shows the variation of potential difference $V$ across the capacitor with time $t$. The gradient of the graph is $G$. What is the capacitance of the capacitor?
[Graph: V against t, straight line through the origin]
A. $\frac{I}{G}$
B. $\frac{G}{I}$
C. $G \times I$
D. $\frac{1}{G \times I}$

37.text_clean:
37. A particle of energy $E$ is incident upon a barrier and has a certain probability of quantum tunnelling through the barrier. Assuming $E$ remains constant, which combination of changes in particle mass and barrier length will increase the probability of the particle tunnelling through the barrier?
Particle mass | Barrier length
A. decrease | decrease
B. increase | decrease
C. decrease | increase
D. increase | increase

38.text_clean:
38. Element X has a nucleon number $A_X$ and a nuclear density $\rho_X$. Element Y has a nucleon number of $2A_X$. What is an estimate of the nuclear density of element Y?
A. $\frac{1}{2}\rho_X$
B. $\rho_X$
C. $2\rho_X$
D. $8\rho_X$

39.text_clean:
39. What is true for the Bohr model for the hydrogen atom?
A. Angular momentum of electrons is quantized.
B. Electrons are described by wave functions.
C. Electrons never exist in fixed orbitals.
D. Electrons will continuously emit radiation.

40.text_clean:
40. An electron of non-relativistic speed $v$ interacts with an atom. All the energy of the electron is transferred to an emitted photon of frequency $f$. An electron of speed $2v$ now interacts with the same atom and all its energy is transmitted to a second photon. What is the frequency of the second photon?
A. $\frac{f}{4}$
B. $\frac{f}{2}$
C. $2f$
D. $4f$
